name: single_sample
_why_schema_version: Mandatory (rule 9), and it matters more here than in the genotyping profile: this file is the second module the schema ever carries, so a reader looking at it cannot yet assume the loader and the file agree about what a step is. A version this build does not implement is a refusal, never a best-effort parse.
_why_callers: Empty on purpose. `callers` is the list an `@`-shaped key fans out over, and this profile binds no `@`-shaped key: upstream's single-sample launch template (`GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.json.tmpl`) binds no per-caller attribute, because the caller fan-out happens inside the WDL. An empty list also makes the loader refuse any future `@` binding instead of expanding it over an unchecked list. This field does not say which tools consume the profile.

freeze._why_attrs: The only per-sample files the step reads off its row (`this.bam_or_cram_file`, `this.case_stripy_file`); every other input is a workspace attribute or a literal. The CRAM/BAM index is not an attribute: GatherSampleEvidence derives it as the read file's path plus `.crai`/`.bai`, so batch_freeze copies that sidecar next to the frozen file. case_stripy_file is optional because the WDL declares it `File?` and many rows do not carry it.
freeze._why_attr_suffix: Empty: the step reads `this.bam_or_cram_file` with no frozen suffix (scripts/selftest.d/profiles.sh v_no_frozen refuses one), so the baseline row in the sandbox carries the frozen copies under the names the step reads.
freeze._why_row_mode: The sandbox has no baseline sample row of its own; the TSV creates it (and merges onto it if it exists), so plan prints the TSV before anything is written.

steps._why_step: The two-digit prefix is REQUIRED, not decorative: `terra/steps.py::_tables` refuses a step whose key does not start with one, because every tool in `terra/` matches a workspace's method configs on that number -- an unnumbered entry is invisible to all of them, which reads exactly like a chain that does not contain the step. What the NUMBER is is a fact upstream does not have: its `NN-` numbering (`01-GatherSampleEvidence` ... `23-AnnotateVcf`) is the COHORT joint-calling chain in `website/docs/execution/joint.md`, and the single-sample flavor ships one launch config template that is not numbered at all (`inputs/templates/terra_workspaces/single_sample/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.json.tmpl`). So `01` is this module's own step-one -- module-local, stated here rather than borrowed -- and it is safe to be module-local because the flavor lives in its own workspace (upstream ships a `single_sample/` flavor with its own `workspace.tsv.tmpl`, `sample.tsv.tmpl` and `participant.tsv.tmpl`, not rows inside the cohort workspace).
steps._why_rootEntityType: `sample` is the CROSS-CHECK, not the answer. The answer is derived from this step's own bindings: `this.sample_id` is the single single-component `this.<etype>_id` read in the map (`kit/module_profile.py::derive_entity_type`, the same rule `checks/terra_entity_check.py` applies to upstream's launch configs), so the type comes from the artifact a launcher posts rather than from a typed string it has to trust. Two independent things agree at `e1909d2f`: the derived stem is `sample`, and the shipped entity table for that flavor -- `inputs/templates/terra_workspaces/single_sample/sample.tsv.tmpl` -- is headed `entity:sample_id`. Upstream's own launch config reads `${this.sample_id}` for BOTH `sample_id` and `batch`, which is why the name key appears twice in the map below and only once as a type.
steps._why_entity_row: `--entity`, the one value that names no config key. Nothing offline holds a SAMPLE row name: `GSVTK_BATCH` names a `sample_set` (the cohort batch row, `all_samples` by default), so it is the wrong KIND for this step, not merely the wrong value -- the same mistake `09-MergeBatchSites` would make if its cohort row came from that key. The row is a sample (upstream's own values profiles name `NA12878`/`NA19240`), the operator names it, and a launcher refuses this step by name rather than defaulting it to a row it was never told.
steps._why_images:
Thirteen of the fourteen *_docker inputs this step binds are left to the command line: their entry is the operator-supplies-it marker, and the run refuses without them. The fourteenth is stated in this file, and the reason it is here rather than left to the flag is at the end of this sentence. No literal refs are committed here on purpose. Upstream ships its own image refs in inputs/values/dockers.json, and copying them into a profile would be the transcription rule 5 exists to stop; the refs that would actually run are per-branch and per-project, so a committed tag is rot plus a leak surface -- the coordinate leg in scripts/selftest.sh evicted a live capture an hour ago for naming one personal tag. A tagged ref IS accepted here, and that is the route for a machine that wants its pins in a file: the loader refuses an untagged ref, a blank, a workspace. or this. value, and any key this step does not bind. `linux_docker` is that fourteenth, stated as a ref with `versioned_by: path`, and this is the first literal
 ref in any profile this repo ships. Upstream's own pinboard carries it as `marketplace.gcr.io/google/ubuntu1804` -- a GCE
 image FAMILY, with no tag and no digest in it -- so nothing can resolve it to an immutable ref, and
 `docker/image_capture.py` has to leave a key like that unresolved rather than invent a version for it. Here
 the path IS where the version lives, and `module_profile.ref_version_kind` honours that declaration only when
 the LAST path segment ends in a version token, which is why the same door stays shut for
 `cloud_sdk_docker`: `google/cloud-sdk` carries no version anywhere, the digit test refuses it, and that is
 correct -- the name floats, and pinning whatever `latest` happened to mean at capture time is the laundering
 that test exists to stop. This is the first literal ref in any profile, and it is here because the
 alternative was a launch that needed `--allow-unpinned-docker` forever to run one family path.
steps._why_inputs: COMPLETE for every binding this ref's launch template carries as a VALUE: 107 of its 111 distinct keys (4 entity reads, 82 workspace paths, 16 literals/arrays, 5 call-level bindings), each a verbatim read of inputs/templates/terra_workspaces/single_sample/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.json.tmpl at gatk-sv e1909d2f with the dollar-brace wrapper stripped from a path and every JSON type untouched. The 4 keys that are not here are not literals upstream either: the template binds them with a Jinja read out of the reference_resources values bundle, they are named in _why_unbound, and rendering them is what docs/module-profiles.md SS4 refuses. So rule 2 -- the input map is the COMPLETE map -- is the one rule this file does not yet satisfy, and `check` names the two required keys among them as MISSING on every run; nothing here makes that hole read as clean.
steps._why_unbound: NOTHING upstream binds that this profile leaves out, measured: the launch template at e1909d2f binds 111 keys and every one of them is in `inputs` here (0 in the difference). This field used to name four keys as unbound -- clustering_track_names and clustering_track_bed_files (both REQUIRED, no WDL default) plus external_af_population and genome_tracks (optional, so they silently took the WDL default) -- and that claim is now false, so it was rewritten rather than left to rot. Six keys come from the live golden capture instead of from the template, and two of them (flank_exclusion_intervals, use_melt) are bound here and NOT by upstream's template: they are declared at 743dd9d4 with defaults, and leaving them out would answer the WDL's default where the run being compared answered the operator. `use_melt` toggles a caller, which is the difference between two sets of evidence, not a cosmetic default. Per-key `_why_*` notes carry each value's provenance.
steps._why_template_overrides: Upstream's template leaves these to the WDL default; the baseline run bound them explicitly, so they are bound here to the baseline's values. Each key's own `_why_` says more.
steps._why_outputs: 15 names, which is the whole `output {}` block of `wdl/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.wdl` at `e1909d2f` (`:1593-1625`), and the reason this map exists at all: upstream's launch templates carry INPUTS ONLY (`grep -c 'output\.'` is 0 on this very template), so a config built from the template binds nothing, Rawls answers `invalidOutputs: 0` for an empty map because there is nothing to invalidate, the workflow runs, succeeds, and throws every result away with the scratch bucket. That is the $18.87 / 20 h incident, and it is why an output map has to be carried here even though no upstream file has one to copy. They are written to `this.<attr>{new}` -- the SAMPLE ROW, one set of results per sample -- because every result in that block is one sample's (`final_vcf`, `metrics_file`, `ploidy_matrix`); `workspace.<attr>` write-back is the cohort pattern this repo carries for `09-MergeBatchSites`, whose row is one cohort. Four of the 15 (`stripy_*`) are `File?` in the WDL, so an attribute stays unwritten when Stripy is not run -- `check` grades the NAME against the declaration, which is the expensive direction, and does not promise the value arrives.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.mei_bed: Bound ONCE, to the value a submission actually gets. Upstream's template binds this key TWICE: `"GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.mei_bed": "${workspace.mei_bed}"` on one line and `"${workspace.reference_mei_bed}"` further down, and `dict`'s last-wins rule drops the first in silence. This is one of the three files at `e1909d2f` that bind a key twice, and `check` names it per step as `DUPLICATE-KEY` with BOTH values. Taking the survivor -- not the earlier read, not a merge -- is the same side a strict `json.loads` takes, so a config built from this map is byte-for-byte the config a strict parse of upstream's document yields; a JSON object cannot carry the second value anyway, so the FACT lives here and in `check`'s output rather than in a second binding. The dropped name is also the unlaunchable one: `mei_bed` is not a row of this flavor's workspace table (`inputs/templates/terra_workspaces/single_sample/workspace.tsv.tmpl` carries `reference_mei_bed` and no `mei_bed`), so `workspace.mei_bed` would resolve to nothing at run time -- Stage B's `UNRESOLVED` for a `${workspace.X}` with no row at that ref.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.RefineCo: One of five CALL-LEVEL bindings (`MakeCohortVcf.HERVK_reference`, `.LINE1_reference`, `.intron_reference`, `RefineComplexVariants.n_per_split`, `AnnotateVcf.par_bed`) -- a three-segment key is Terra's way of wiring an input into a CALL inside the workflow, and it is legitimate wiring, not a typo in the top-level map. `check` reports each as `UNCHECKED ... binds a call into 'RefineComplexVariants'` and does NOT grade it, because comparing it needs that callee's own declared inputs and `check_maps` reads the top-level workflow's only (the same three-state discipline the output side keeps as `out UNCHECKED`); they are carried here because rule 2's unit is what production binds, and upstream binds them. `n_per_split` is the STRING "15000" on the wire while the callee takes an Int -- Cromwell coerces it, and the type recorded here is the one that travels, the same rule that keeps step 07's `N_IQR_cutoff_plotting` as the string "6" in profiles/genotyping.json.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.clusteri: Required array with no default (wdl/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.wdl:409-410 at 743dd9d4) and NOT bound by upstream's workspace template, so `check --against 743dd9d4` reported it MISSING and a config without it fails at launch, not at create. The value was read off the live golden capture (recon-live/; see scripts/selftest.d/golden/README.md) because nothing in the ref derives it -- this is the one value in this profile taken from a real workspace rather than derived, stated here because a later reader cannot recover it from the file. If the ref grows a default, this note is stale and the entry should go.

Array[File] twin of clustering_track_names: required, no default, unbound upstream, value from the live golden capture for the same reason. The paths are the public gatk-sv-resources bucket, one per track name (SR/SD/RM) -- the pairing is what the WDL's `track_names`/`bed_files` zips, so the two entries must move together or clustering silently loses a track.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.use_melt: Declared at 743dd9d4 WITH a default, so `check` is clean without it -- but the golden binds it explicitly, so leaving it unbound means this launch answers the WDL's default where the run being compared answered the operator. Value taken from the live golden capture (recon-live/) for that reason. This one toggles a caller, so a default here is the difference between two different sets of evidence, not a cosmetic default.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.genome_t: Declared at 743dd9d4 WITH a default, so `check` is clean without it -- but the golden binds it explicitly, so leaving it unbound means this launch answers the WDL's default where the run being compared answered the operator. Value taken from the live golden capture (recon-live/) for that reason. Plotting/track inputs.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.external: Declared at 743dd9d4 WITH a default, so `check` is clean without it -- but the golden binds it explicitly, so leaving it unbound means this launch answers the WDL's default where the run being compared answered the operator. Value taken from the live golden capture (recon-live/) for that reason. Population AF source used by filtering/annotation.
steps._why_GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.flank_ex: Declared at 743dd9d4 WITH a default, so `check` is clean without it -- but the golden binds it explicitly, so leaving it unbound means this launch answers the WDL's default where the run being compared answered the operator. Value taken from the live golden capture (recon-live/) for that reason. Exclusion intervals used by filtering.
steps._why_workflow: 'workflow' is the Dockstore ENTRY name, not the WDL file name, and for this module they differ: .github/.dockstore.yml:256-257 publishes /wdl/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.wdl under the name 'SingleSamplePipeline'. The live golden agrees -- its methodRepoMethod.methodUri is dockstore://github.com%2Fbroadinstitute%2Fgatk-sv%2FSingleSamplePipeline/<version>. This profile said 'GATKSVPipelineSingleSample' first, which is a Dockstore entry that does not exist: the config would have been created pointing at nothing and the submission would fail downstream, after compute was requested. Caught by comparing the printed body against the live capture before the POST.
steps._why_dockstore: 'dockstore' is the Dockstore ENTRY the method resolves from, and for this module it is NOT the WDL name: .github/.dockstore.yml:256-257 publishes /wdl/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.wdl under the name 'SingleSamplePipeline', and the live golden's methodRepoMethod.methodUri agrees (dockstore://github.com%2Fbroadinstitute%2Fgatk-sv%2FSingleSamplePipeline/<version>). Everything else -- the WDL file, the binding-key prefix, the config name -- is keyed on 'workflow' (which is the name the WDL's own 'workflow GATKSVPipelineSingleSample {' block declares, wdl/GATKSVPipelineSingleSample.wdl:35). A launch that used 'workflow' for the method path would POST a config pointing at a Dockstore entry that does not exist.
steps._why_literals: Terra stores these as literals; upstream's .json.tmpl stores `workspace.<attr>` and expects the operator's own setup to have populated the workspace attributes first. The target workspace has not, so a launch that kept the template's indirection was rejected at submission -- `HTTP 400 Validation errors: Invalid inputs` -- after the config had passed `validate` (validate typechecks against the WDL and never resolves a workspace attribute, so a clean validate is not evidence a submission will be accepted). Every value here was read from recon-live/live-config-01-SingleSample-devfix.json, the live capture of the run this launch is meant to compare against, not typed. Taking them as literals is also this repo's standing rule: a launch that inherits its resources from workspace attributes cannot state what it ran. No `*_docker` key belongs here: those are graded by the image rule (--image, or a tagged ref stated once in steps[].images). The capture's own `sv_pipeline_docker` was a personal registry path carrying a username, so a literal for it would have made the wrong code the default when no --image was given.
